findings.title: Missing prisma import causes ReferenceError
findings.body: File uses prisma.credential.update at line 96 but there is no import of @calcom/prisma in the file. Any instantiation of SalesforceCalendarService will throw ReferenceError: prisma is not defined when getClient() runs, breaking all Salesforce operations.

findings.title: Refreshed Salesforce token never used for connection
findings.body: getClient() fetches a new token and persists accessTokenParsed.data to the DB, but then constructs the jsforce.Connection with the old credentialKey.instance_url/accessToken/refreshToken instead of the newly parsed values. The refresh is therefore wasted and the client continues to use the expired access token.

findings.title: Salesforce refresh checks statusText instead of ok
findings.body: Line 86 throws only if response.statusText !== "OK". With fetch, statusText is often empty or implementation-dependent even on success, and non-2xx responses can have arbitrary text. The check should be !response.ok / status code. As written valid refreshes can throw and invalid refreshes can pass through to JSON parsing.

findings.title: Minimum token schema uses invalid computed keys
findings.body: minimumTokenResponseSchema is declared with [z.string().toString()] as object keys, which evaluates to a literal string like "[object Object]" instead of a catch-all. Zod does not support dynamic string keys that way. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is on, validation does not mean what the comment says and legitimate minimal {access_token, expiry} payloads can fail or pass incorrectly.

findings.title: Dummy refresh_token placeholder corrupts stored credentials
findings.body: If the parsed payload has no refresh_token the code injects the literal string "refresh_token" and callers persist it. Subsequent real OAuth refreshes will then send refresh_token="refresh_token" to the provider and fail, and Google/Office/Zoom code paths that merge tokenResponse.data will overwrite a valid stored refresh token with the placeholder.

findings.title: Sync branch returns fetch Response incompatible with callers
findings.body: When credential sync is enabled the helper returns a raw fetch Response from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT. Callers expect provider-specific shapes: Google expects {data:{access_token,expiry_date}}, HubSpot expects a HubspotToken object, Zoho/Bigin expect an axios response with .data. For example HubSpot casts the result directly to HubspotToken and reads .expiresIn, and Google reads res?.data, so the sync path yields undefined/NaN tokens and breaks refresh for those integrations.

findings.title: Bigin passes credentialId as userId to sync endpoint
findings.body: refreshOAuthTokens expects (fn, appSlug, userId) and sends it as calcomUserId to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT. Bigin calls it with credentialId (credential.id) instead of credential.userId. The remote endpoint receives a credential ID where it expects a user ID, causing wrong-user lookups and leaking/mixing tokens across users.

findings.title: Webhook has no method check and unhandled validation errors
findings.body: Handler accepts any HTTP method and calls appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse without try/catch. Invalid bodies throw a ZodError that becomes an unhandled 500 instead of a 400, and GET/DELETE can create/update credentials. Also symmetricDecrypt/JSON.parse can throw unhandled. The endpoint should restrict to POST and return 400 on validation/decryption failure.
